subject: Performance packaging and MAP timeline for close - Acme Cloud
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Todd <elaine.todd@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance packaging and MAP timeline for close - Acme Cloud

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the call today — this thread is to confirm the MAP items we discussed and the packaging plan for the performance artifacts you'll need for procurement and the exec readout. Attached is a working checklist (acme_map_checklist_v1.xlsx) and an initial slide draft.

High-level plan (requesting sign-off):
- Benchmark window: Mon 2027-03-22 through Wed 2027-03-24 (concurrency and steady-state runs)
- Primary metrics: median latency, P95 latency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), tokens/sec throughput at target concurrency
- Deliverables by Thu 2027-03-25:
  - Executive slides (PDF/PPTX) summarizing results and risk areas
  - CSV exports of raw traces (ttft_concurrency_results_20270318.csv format)
  - Read-only dashboard link with filters and annotations

Ask: please confirm the TTFT / latency SLOs you care about so we can prioritize runs. In our meeting you mentioned TTFT ~ 120ms and P95 < 450ms for the interactive flow — is that still accurate? Also please confirm any legal or procurement items that should be in the executive pack.

I'll loop in Vivek and Laura on the exec deck and packaging. If that timeline is tight for your side we can shift the readout to the week of 3/29.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_map_checklist_v1.xlsx, acme_perf_slides_draft_v1.pptx
From: Elaine Todd <elaine.todd@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance packaging and MAP timeline for close - Acme Cloud

Thanks Evelyn — confirmed on receiving the checklist. A few notes from the Acme side:

- TTFT target: 120ms (interactive search path) — yes, please prioritize TTFT first.
- Concurrency target: steady-state 40 concurrent sessions; burst tests up to 120 for 30s windows.
- For procurement: we need CSV exports of raw per-request traces and a simple artifact naming convention that includes date and model hash.
- Can you provide a short-lived test account and API key scoped to the Acme project for us to validate the CSVs after you deliver them?

Can you also make sure the slides include the fallback plan (model variant + routing) and the cost delta table for quantized vs full precision runs — procurement will flag that.

If the 3/25 deliverable date is firm on your side, we'll aim for an internal dry-run on 3/26 and schedule the executive readout in our calendar.

—Elaine
Elaine Todd
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Todd <elaine.todd@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance packaging and MAP timeline for close - Acme Cloud

Vivek / Laura — looping you both to confirm internal owners for packaging and the exec readout. Elaine has confirmed targets; key asks below.

Owner suggestions: 
- Vivek: executive readout + cost delta table (you have the prior pricing comps)
- Laura: slides and dashboard annotations (Laura, can you create the slides from the draft and add notes for each result?)
- Evelyn: coordinate the benchmark runs and deliver CSV exports + Drive folder organization

Deliverable checklist (we will attach final files to the MAP and to HubSpot):
1) Executive slides (PDF + PPTX) — concise (6–8 slides) with top-line metrics and fallbacks
2) Raw CSVs: ttft_concurrency_results_<date>.csv + run metadata (model id, kernel, sequence len)
3) Dashboard link with pre-set time windows and comments
4) Short README (1-pager) describing how to interpret the CSV columns and extraction queries

Notes: we should include a small appendix slide showing variance across 3 repeated runs to head off questions about single-run flukes. Also add a one-line statement about data retention and logs for compliance.

Elaine — can you confirm a 30–45 minute slot for an exec readout either Thu 3/25 afternoon or Mon 3/29 morning PT? If you prefer, we can do a 15-minute top-line and follow with a technical deep dive for Eng.

Thanks — I'll start the runs Monday morning and share preliminary CSVs on Wed.

Evelyn
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Todd <elaine.todd@acme.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance packaging and MAP timeline for close - Acme Cloud

Elaine — quick note from our side: we completed the benchmark packaging and uploaded artifacts. Links below.

Deliverables (uploaded 2027-03-21):
- Exec slides (final): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XyZ_acme_perf_slides_final
- Raw CSV exports: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDefG_acme_map_perf (files prefixed ttft_concurrency_results_20270321.csv)
- Dashboard (read-only): https://dash.redwood.ai/acme-cloud/benchmarks/rd-acme-2027-042 (use view-only key RDVIEW-ACME-03)
- README: included in the Drive folder (README_interpreting_results.txt)

Top-line summary:
- Median TTFT (interactive path): 118ms
- P95 latency: 430ms
- Sustained throughput at 40 conc: 3600 tokens/sec
- Burst at 120 conc (30s window): peak aggregate 9800 tokens/sec; transient P95 spikes to ~760ms (see appendix)

Next steps: please confirm a slot for the exec readout. We can do Thu 3/25 3:00–3:30pm PT (preferred) or Mon 3/29 9:00–9:45am PT. Also confirming: Evelyn will provide the API key for your validation account and the CSV naming convention includes model hash and run id as requested.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: ttft_concurrency_results_20270321.csv (in Drive)
